100	class CircuitState:
101	    """The register state of one circuit, keyed by register name."""
102	
103	    def __init__(self, cells: Optional[Sequence[RegisterCell]] = None) -> None:
104	        self.cells: Dict[str, RegisterCell] = {}
105	        for cell in cells or ():
106	            self.cells[cell.name] = cell
107	
108	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
109	    @classmethod
110	    def from_module(
111	        cls, module: Operation, rules: Optional[RuleSet] = None
112	    ) -> "CircuitState":
113	        """Discover every register in ``module``'s body.
114	
115	        A "register" is any operation the rule set gives a *sequential* rule, so
116	        adding a stateful operation to the semantics automatically teaches the
117	        executor about it.
118	        """
119	        rule_set = rules if rules is not None else CIRCUIT_RULES
120	        cells: List[RegisterCell] = []
121	        for op in _body_operations(module):
122	            if not rule_set.rules_for(op.name, RulePhase.SEQUENTIAL):
123	                continue
124	            cells.append(
125	                RegisterCell(
126	                    name=register_key(op),
127	                    width=_width_of_op(op),
128	                    reset_value=_reset_value_of(op),
129	                    op=op,
130	                )
131	            )
132	        state = cls(cells)
133	        state.reset()
134	        return state
135	
136	    # -- access -----------------------------------------------------------
137	    def cell(self, name: str) -> Optional[RegisterCell]:
138	        return self.cells.get(name)
139	
140	    def read(self, name: str, default: int = 0) -> int:
141	        cell = self.cells.get(name)
142	        return cell.value if cell is not None else int(default)
143	
144	    def write(self, name: str, value: int) -> int:
145	        cell = self.cells.get(name)
146	        if cell is None:
147	            cell = self.cells.setdefault(name, RegisterCell(name=name))
148	        return cell.write(value)
149	
150	    def stage(self, name: str, value: int) -> int:
151	        cell = self.cells.get(name)
152	        if cell is None:
153	            cell = self.cells.setdefault(name, RegisterCell(name=name))
154	        return cell.stage(value)
155	
156	    def commit(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
157	        return {name: cell.commit() for name, cell in self.cells.items()}
158	
159	    def reset(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
160	        return {name: cell.reset() for name, cell in self.cells.items()}
161	
162	    # -- views -------------------------------------------------------------
163	    def snapshot(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
164	        return {name: cell.value for name, cell in self.cells.items()}
165	
166	    def names(self) -> List[str]:
167	        return list(self.cells)
168	
169	    @property
170	    def registers(self) -> List[RegisterCell]:
171	        return list(self.cells.values())
172	
173	    @property
174	    def is_stateful(self) -> bool:
175	        return bool(self.cells)
176	
177	    # -- configuration interop --------------------------------------------
178	    def load_into(self, config: KConfiguration) -> KConfiguration:
179	        """Copy this state into a configuration's ``<state>`` cell."""
180	        config.state.clear()
181	        config.state.update(self.snapshot())
182	        return config
183	
184	    def sync_from(self, config: KConfiguration) -> "CircuitState":
185	        """Adopt the values a rule left in ``<state>``."""
186	        for name, value in config.state.items():
187	            self.write(name, value)
188	        return self
189	
190	    def __len__(self) -> int:
191	        return len(self.cells)
192	
193	    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[RegisterCell]:
194	        return iter(self.cells.values())
195	
196	    def __contains__(self, name: str) -> bool:
197	        return name in self.cells
198	
199	    def __str__(self) -> str:
200	        return " ".join(str(cell) for cell in self.cells.values()) or ".Map"
201	
202	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging helper
203	        return f"<CircuitState registers={list(self.cells)}>"
204

211	def _body_operations(module: Operation) -> List[Operation]:
212	    if not module.regions or not module.regions[0].blocks:
213	        return []
214	    return list(module.regions[0].blocks[0].operations)
215	
216	
217	def _width_of_op(op: Operation) -> int:
218	    from circt.hw_dialect import bit_width_of
219	
220	    for result in op.results:
221	        width = bit_width_of(result.type)
222	        if width:
223	            return width
224	    return int(getattr(op, "_declared_width", 0) or 0)
225	
226	
227	def _reset_value_of(op: Operation) -> int:
228	    """The register's power-on value.
229	
230	    ``seq.compreg %next, %clk reset %reset, %c0_i8`` names its reset value with
231	    an operand, so the constant behind that operand is read directly - the reset
232	    value has to be known before any rule has settled the design.  The operand
233	    index comes from the dialect class (``seq.compreg.ce`` puts a clock enable
234	    before the reset pair), defaulting to CIRCT's plain-register layout.
235	    """
236	    declared = int(getattr(op, "reset_value", 0) or 0)
237	    index = int(getattr(op, "RESET_VALUE", 3))
238	    operands = op.operands
239	    if len(operands) <= index:
240	        return declared
241	    operand = operands[index]
242	    if not isinstance(operand, Value):
243	        return declared
244	    defining = operand.defining_op
245	    if defining is None:
246	        return declared
247	    attr = defining.attributes.get("value")
248	    if attr is None or not defining.has_trait(Trait.CONSTANT_LIKE):
249	        return declared
250	    try:
251	        return int(attr.value)
252	    except (TypeError, ValueError):  # pragma: no cover - defensive
253	        return declared

261	@dataclass
262	class CycleResult:
263	    """Everything one clock cycle produced."""
264	
265	    cycle: int
266	    inputs: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
267	    outputs: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
268	    registers: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
269	    next_registers: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
270	    applications: List[RuleApplication] = field(default_factory=list)
271	
272	    @property
273	    def num_steps(self) -> int:
274	        return len(self.applications)
275	
276	    def rule_names(self) -> List[str]:
277	        return [application.rule for application in self.applications]
278	
279	    def output(self, name: Optional[str] = None, default: int = 0) -> int:
280	        if name is None:
281	            return next(iter(self.outputs.values()), default)
282	        return self.outputs.get(name, default)
283	
284	    def __str__(self) -> str:
285	        parts = [f"cycle={self.cycle}"]
286	        for label, values in (
287	            ("in", self.inputs),
288	            ("state", self.registers),
289	            ("out", self.outputs),
290	        ):
291	            if values:
292	                rendered = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(values.items()))
293	                parts.append(f"{label}({rendered})")
294	        parts.append(f"steps={self.num_steps}")
295	        return " ".join(parts)

303	class StatefulCircuit:
304	    """Executes an ``hw.module`` through the semantic rules, cycle by cycle."""
305	
306	    def __init__(
307	        self,
308	        module: Operation,
309	        rules: Optional[RuleSet] = None,
310	        engine: Optional[RuleEngine] = None,
311	    ) -> None:
312	        if module.name not in MODULE_OPS:
313	            raise SemanticError(
314	                f"expected a hardware module operation, got '{module.name}'"
315	            )
316	        self.module = module
317	        self.rules = rules if rules is not None else CIRCUIT_RULES
318	        self.engine = engine if engine is not None else RuleEngine(self.rules)
319	        self.config = KConfiguration.initial()
320	        self.state = CircuitState.from_module(module, self.rules)
321	
322	        self._body: List[Operation] = _body_operations(module)
323	        self._ports = list(getattr(module, "ports", []) or [])
324	        self._input_ports = [p for p in self._ports if not p.is_output]
325	        self._output_ports = [p for p in self._ports if p.is_output]
326	        self._registers = [
327	            cell.op for cell in self.state.registers if cell.op is not None
328	        ]
329	        self.inputs: Dict[str, int] = {p.name: 0 for p in self._input_ports}
330	        self.reset()
331	
332	    # -- structure --------------------------------------------------------
333	    @property
334	    def ports(self) -> List[Any]:
335	        return list(self._ports)
336	
337	    @property
338	    def input_names(self) -> List[str]:
339	        return [p.name for p in self._input_ports]
340	
341	    @property
342	    def output_names(self) -> List[str]:
343	        return [p.name for p in self._output_ports]
344	
345	    @property
346	    def body(self) -> List[Operation]:
347	        return list(self._body)
348	
349	    @property
350	    def registers(self) -> List[RegisterCell]:
351	        return self.state.registers
352	
353	    @property
354	    def is_sequential(self) -> bool:
355	        return self.state.is_stateful
356	
357	    @property
358	    def cycle(self) -> int:
359	        return self.config.cycle
360	
361	    # -- lifecycle --------------------------------------------------------
362	    def reset(self) -> "StatefulCircuit":
363	        """Assert reset: clear the configuration and re-seed register state."""
364	        self.config.reset()
365	        self.state.reset()
366	        self.state.load_into(self.config)
367	        self.engine.reset()
368	        return self
369	
370	    def set_input(self, name: str, value: int) -> None:
371	        if name not in self.inputs:
372	            raise SemanticError(f"'{name}' is not an input port of this module")
373	        self.inputs[name] = int(value)
374	
375	    def set_inputs(self, values: Optional[Dict[str, int]]) -> None:
376	        for name, value in (values or {}).items():
377	            self.set_input(name, value)
378	
379	    # -- phase 1: combinational settle ------------------------------------
380	    def settle(
381	        self, inputs: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None
382	    ) -> List[RuleApplication]:
383	        """Bind the ports, then drain ``<k>`` with the combinational rules."""
384	        self.set_inputs(inputs)
385	        self._seed_environment()
386	        return self.engine.settle(self.config, self._body)
387	
388	    def _seed_environment(self) -> None:
389	        config = self.config
390	        config.cell("env").clear()
391	        config.cell("outputs").clear()
392	        config.inputs.clear()
393	        config.inputs.update(self.inputs)
394	        self.state.load_into(config)
395	
396	        block = self._entry_block()
397	        if block is None:
398	            return
399	        for index, argument in enumerate(block.arguments):
400	            name = (
401	                self._input_ports[index].name
402	                if index < len(self._input_ports)
403	                else (argument.name or f"arg{index}")
404	            )
405	            value = int(self.inputs.get(name, 0))
406	            config.bind(argument, value)
407	            if name:
408	                config.bind(name, value)
409	
410	    def _entry_block(self) -> Optional[Block]:
411	        if not self.module.regions or not self.module.regions[0].blocks:
412	            return None
413	        return self.module.regions[0].blocks[0]
414	
415	    # -- phase 2: clock edge ----------------------------------------------
416	    def step(self, inputs: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None) -> CycleResult:
417	        """Advance one clock cycle and report what happened."""
418	        applications = list(self.settle(inputs))
419	        before = self.state.snapshot()
420	        outputs = dict(self.config.outputs)
421	
422	        applications.extend(self.engine.latch(self.config, self._registers))
423	        staged = dict(self.config.next_state)
424	        cycle = self.config.cycle
425	        applications.append(self.engine.clock_edge(self.config))
426	        self.state.sync_from(self.config)
427	
428	        return CycleResult(
429	            cycle=cycle,
430	            inputs=dict(self.inputs),
431	            outputs=outputs,
432	            registers=before,
433	            next_registers=staged,
434	            applications=applications,
435	        )
436	
437	    def run(
438	        self,
439	        cycles: int,
440	        inputs: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None,
441	        stimulus: Optional[Sequence[Dict[str, int]]] = None,
442	    ) -> List[CycleResult]:
443	        """Run ``cycles`` clock cycles, returning one result per cycle."""
444	        self.set_inputs(inputs)
445	        results: List[CycleResult] = []
446	        for index in range(max(0, cycles)):
447	            override = None
448	            if stimulus is not None and index < len(stimulus):
449	                override = stimulus[index]
450	            results.append(self.step(override))
451	        return results
452	
453	    # -- reading results --------------------------------------------------
454	    def evaluate(self, inputs: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None) -> Dict[str, int]:
455	        """Settle without a clock edge and return the module outputs."""
456	        self.settle(inputs)
457	        return dict(self.config.outputs)
458	
459	    def output(self, name: Optional[str] = None, default: int = 0) -> int:
460	        outputs = self.config.outputs
461	        if name is None:
462	            return next(iter(outputs.values()), default)
463	        if name not in outputs:
464	            raise SemanticError(f"'{name}' is not an output port of this module")
465	        return outputs[name]
466	
467	    def output_after(
468	        self,
469	        cycles: int,
470	        inputs: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None,
471	        name: Optional[str] = None,
472	    ) -> int:
473	        """Run ``cycles`` cycles, settle once more, then read an output."""
474	        self.run(cycles, inputs)
475	        self.settle()
476	        return self.output(name)
477	
478	    def register_values(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
479	        return self.state.snapshot()
480	
481	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging helper
482	        symbol = self.module.attributes.get("sym_name")
483	        label = symbol.value if symbol is not None else "?"
484	        return (
485	            f"<StatefulCircuit @{label} ports={len(self._ports)} "
486	            f"registers={len(self.state)} cycle={self.cycle}>"
487	        )
488

491	# Functional (arith / func) execution
492	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
493	
494	
495	def execute_function(
496	    func: Operation,
497	    arguments: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None,
498	    rules: Optional[RuleSet] = None,
499	) -> Dict[str, int]:
500	    """Evaluate a ``func.func`` body through the same rules.
501	
502	    This is what connects the semantic layer back to the MLIR sample input: the
503	    ``arith`` rules in :mod:`src.k_circt.semantics` evaluate ``@fold_chain``
504	    without the circuit machinery being involved at all.  Multi-block bodies work
505	    too - the ``cf`` rules rewrite the ``<k>`` cell to the successor's body, so
506	    ``@multi_block`` follows its ``cf.cond_br`` the way the CFG says it should.
507	    """
508	    if func.name not in ("func.func", "builtin.func"):
509	        raise SemanticError(f"expected a function operation, got '{func.name}'")
510	    if not func.regions or not func.regions[0].blocks:
511	        return {}
512	
513	    engine = RuleEngine(rules if rules is not None else CIRCUIT_RULES)
514	    config = KConfiguration.initial()
515	    block = func.regions[0].blocks[0]
516	
517	    supplied = list(arguments or ())
518	    for index, argument in enumerate(block.arguments):
519	        value = supplied[index] if index < len(supplied) else 0
520	        config.bind(argument, int(value))
521	        if argument.name:
522	            config.bind(argument.name, int(value))
523	
524	    config.enqueue_all(list(block.operations))
525	    engine.run(config, RulePhase.FUNCTIONAL)
526	    return dict(config.outputs)

20	class BranchOp(Operation):

26	    def __init__(

28	        dest: Optional[Block] = None,
29	        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,

31	        name: Optional[str] = None,

49	        if len(self.successors) != 1:
50	            return [f"'{self.name}' expects exactly one successor"]
